block.ee_extras.three_phase_rectifier.to: Three phases in, direct current out, rated 6 kW (heats up above that and burns out under a long overload; more headroom in oil). A plain load for the grid, steady output at any speed.
Copper terminals: phases 1-3, red: +, blue: -. No neutral needed.
block.ee_extras.single_phase_rectifier.t: Phase and neutral in, direct current out, rated 6 kW (heats up above that; more headroom in oil). The input is averaged over 2 seconds.
Copper terminals: phase and neutral (either way), red: +, blue: -.
Two converters in one: charges the FE block below (an IE capacitor) from the EE grid and feeds it back to the grid at the same time.
Terminals by the down arrow: charge (EE in); by the up arrow: discharge (EE out, voltage set by the scroll on top). The IE capacitor needs an input side and an output side.
block.ee_extras.four_core_termination.to: From regular wires to a four-core cable: three phases and neutral.
Terminals: brown L1, black L2, grey L3, blue N. The cable goes to the rubber gland.
block.ee_extras.duplex_cable_insulator.t: Support and junction for duplex cable: every cable attached is joined core to core.
Regular wires do not attach. Crafts back into a connector.
block.ee_extras.four_core_cable_insulato: Support and junction for four-core cable: every cable attached is joined core to core.
Regular wires do not attach. Crafts back into two connectors.
block.ee_extras.electric_lantern.tooltip: Click a placed lantern with an EE duplex wire spool to hook it to the EE grid. It becomes a cable junction: every cable on it is joined core to core, so lanterns can be chained in a line.
Lights from 50 V (1000 Ohm: 53 W at 230 V), DC or AC. Breaks back into an IE lantern.
ee_extras.lantern.ie_wired: Remove the IE wires from the lantern first
item.ee_extras.four_core_cable_spool.too: Click one termination or insulator, then another. A four-core block can feed a duplex termination: neutral and one phase, switched with a wrench on the termination.
ee_extras.cable.needs_duplex: Duplex cable only goes to duplex terminations and their insulators
ee_extras.cable.needs_four_core: Four-core cable goes to four-core blocks (one end may be a duplex termination)
ee_extras.cable.lost_selection: The first block of the cable is gone, start again
ee_extras.cable.same_block: A cable cannot loop back to the same block
ee_extras.cable.exists: These blocks are already connected by a cable
ee_extras.cable.no_nodes: Could not attach the cable to the block
ee_extras.nodes.discharge_positive: Discharge + (capacitor out to the EE grid)
ee_extras.nodes.discharge_negative: Discharge - (capacitor out to the EE grid)
ee_extras.cable.rotate_wired: Remove the wires and cable first: rotating an EE termination would break them
ee_extras.cable.selected: Selected: click the second block (Shift + click cancels)
ee_extras.cable.accepts.ee: Duplex cable, or four-core (neutral and one phase)
item.ee_extras.copper_busbar_spool.toolt: Short rigid high-current link: generator to transformer and switchboard.
item.ee_extras.power_cable_spool.tooltip: Copper in thick insulation up to 10 kV: high current in workshops and from generators, short spans. Overheating burns the insulation.
item.ee_extras.stranded_copper_spool.too: Bare line conductor with the lowest losses. Heavy: tensions only a little.
item.ee_extras.acsr_spool.tooltip: The workhorse of long lines: aluminium conducts, the steel core holds long spans and high tension.
item.ee_extras.aluminum_spool.tooltip: Cheap line without a core: shorter spans, more sag.
item.ee_extras.bronze_spool.tooltip: Lines before aluminium: strong, long spans, but noticeable losses.
item.ee_extras.steel_spool.tooltip: Longest spans and almost no sag, but high losses: for low power.
item.ee_extras.tension_clamp.tooltip: Click a line conductor (or EE iron wire): the clamp goes on the nearest end and tensions the wire as far as the material allows. Remove it with a Create wrench; the wire slackens.
ee_extras.line.sag_tension: sag %s%% of span, %s%% with a tension clamp
ee_extras.tension.not_tensionable: This wire cannot take a tension clamp: only line conductors and iron wire
ee_extras.tension.already: This wire already has a tension clamp
block.ee_extras.four_core_tap.tooltip: Four-core cable to phase and neutral for regular EE wires: a single-phase load off a three-phase line.
block.ee_extras.four_core_tap.tooltip.no: Brown terminal: phase, blue: neutral, the cable goes to the rubber gland. Wrench with a cable attached: next phase (L1 → L2 → L3); without one: rotate.
block.ee_extras.heavy_three_phase_rectif: Three phases in, direct current out, rated 48 kW: radiators and bushings. Heats up above rating and burns out under a long overload; more headroom in oil.
Copper caps: phases 1-3, red: +, blue: -. No neutral needed.
block.ee_extras.heavy_single_phase_recti: Phase and neutral in, direct current out, rated 48 kW. Heats up above rating; more headroom in oil. The input is averaged over 2 seconds.
Copper caps: phase and neutral (either way), red: +, blue: -.
block.ee_extras.three_phase_inverter.too: Direct current to three phases in step with the grid, rated 6 kW. Feeds the grid when the DC voltage × 1.05 is above the grid line voltage; with no grid it makes its own 1 Hz AC.
Copper terminals: phases 1-3 (to the grid), red: +, blue: - (from a battery or converter).
block.ee_extras.single_phase_inverter.to: Direct current to phase and neutral in step with the grid, rated 6 kW. Feeds the grid when the DC voltage × 1.57 is above the grid amplitude; with no grid it makes its own 1 Hz AC.
Copper terminals: phase and neutral (to the grid), red: +, blue: - (from a battery or converter).
block.ee_extras.heavy_three_phase_invert: Direct current to three phases in step with the grid, rated 48 kW. Feeds the grid when the DC voltage × 1.05 is above the grid line voltage; with no grid it makes its own 1 Hz AC.
Copper caps: phases 1-3 (to the grid), red: +, blue: - (from a battery or converter).
block.ee_extras.heavy_single_phase_inver: Direct current to phase and neutral in step with the grid, rated 48 kW. Feeds the grid when the DC voltage × 1.57 is above the grid amplitude; with no grid it makes its own 1 Hz AC.
Copper caps: phase and neutral (to the grid), red: +, blue: - (from a battery or converter).
block.ee_extras.compact_kinetic_generato: Create shaft to direct current: 6 W and 0.5 V per RPM (1.5 kW at 128 V at 256 RPM), shaft load 8 SU per RPM. Rated 1.2 kW: above ~200 RPM at full load it smokes.
Shaft at the back face; red terminal: +, blue: -.
